Title: Valid admin login
Preconditions: Test DB configured, Admin credentials in .env.test.local
Steps:
1. Navigate to /login
2. Enter username: admin
3. Enter password: oilbiz2024
4. Click Login button
Expected Result: User logged in successfully, redirected to dashboard, oil_admin_auth cookie set

Title: Invalid username
Steps:
1. Enter username: wronguser
2. Enter password: oilbiz2024
3. Click Login
Expected Result: Login fails with 'Invalid credentials' error, Status 401

Title: Invalid password
Steps:
1. Enter username: admin
2. Enter password: wrongpass
3. Click Login
Expected Result: Login fails with 'Invalid credentials' error, Status 401

Title: Empty credentials
Steps:
1. Leave username and password empty
2. Click Login
Expected Result: Login fails, validation error or 401 response

Title: Rate limit enforcement
Steps:
1. Attempt login with wrong password 5 times
2. Attempt 6th login
Expected Result: After 5 failed attempts, 6th attempt returns 429 status with 'Too many attempts' message

Title: Unauthenticated API access
Steps: 1. Send GET request to /api/customers without auth cookie
Expected Result: Returns 401 Unauthorized error

Title: Token expiry
Preconditions: Logged in, manually set expired token
Steps:
1. Set oil_admin_auth cookie with expired timestamp
2. Access any protected route
Expected Result: Redirected to login or 401 response

Title: Create new customer
Steps: 1. POST /api/customers with {name: 'Test Customer', area: 'Test Area', phone: '1234567890', vehicle_number: 'KA01AB1234'}
Expected Result: Customer created successfully with 201 status, returns customer object with UUID

Title: Get all customers
Preconditions: Logged in, at least 1 customer exists
Expected Result: Returns array of customers, status 200

Title: Search customer by name
Expected Result: Returns filtered customers matching 'Test' in name

Title: Update customer
Steps: 1. PUT /api/customers with {id: <customer_id>, name: 'Updated Name', area: 'New Area', phone: '9999999999', vehicle_number: 'KA02XY5678'}
Expected Result: Customer updated successfully, returns updated customer object

Title: Delete customer
Expected Result: Customer deleted, returns {success: true}

Title: Get customer by ID
Expected Result: Returns single customer object matching ID

Title: Get next invoice number
Preconditions: Logged in, Test DB with bills
Expected Result: Returns invoice number in format ET-{MM}-{N} where MM is current month, N is sequential

Title: Sequential numbering
Steps:
1. GET /api/invoice-number
2. Create bill with returned number
3. GET /api/invoice-number again
Expected Result: Second call returns ET-10-6 (incremented by 1)

Title: Numeric sequencing after 9
Expected Result: Returns ET-10-10 (not ET-10-10 sorted after ET-10-9 alphabetically)

Title: Create bill with single item
Steps: 1. POST /api/bills with {bill_number: 'ET-10-100', customer_id: '<id>', customer_name: 'Test', date: '2026-10-12', items: [{oil_type_id: 'oil1', oil_name: 'Coconut Oil', quantity: 10, rate: 100}], amount_paid: 500}
Expected Result: Bill created with 201 status, total_amount: 1000, amount_paid: 500, due_amount: 500

Title: Create bill with multiple items
Steps: 1. POST /api/bills with 3 items: [{oil_name: 'Oil A', quantity: 5, rate: 100}, {oil_name: 'Oil B', quantity: 10, rate: 50}, {oil_name: 'Oil C', quantity: 2, rate: 250}]
Expected Result: Bill created, total_amount correctly calculated as 1500 (500+500+500)

Title: Bill with zero quantity
Expected Result: Returns 400 error 'Item quantity must be greater than 0'

Title: Bill with negative rate
Expected Result: Returns 400 error 'Item rate cannot be negative'

Title: Bill with empty items array
Expected Result: Returns 400 error 'At least one item is required'

Title: Bill with huge numbers
Expected Result: Bill created, total calculated correctly (999998000001) without overflow

Title: Edit bill items
Expected Result: Bill items updated, total_amount recalculated, due_amount adjusted based on existing payments

Title: Add payment to bill
Preconditions: Logged in, bill with due > 0 exists
Steps: 1. PUT /api/bills with {action: 'add_payment', id: '<bill_id>', payment: {date: '2026-10-12', amount: 200, note: 'Partial payment'}}
Expected Result: Payment added to payments array, amount_paid increased, due_amount decreased

Title: Delete payment from bill
Preconditions: Logged in, bill with payments exists
Expected Result: Payment removed, amount_paid and due_amount recalculated

Title: Get bills by date range
Preconditions: Logged in, bills exist across different dates
Expected Result: Returns only bills within specified date range

Title: Filter bills with dues only
Preconditions: Logged in, bills with due_amount > 0 exist
Expected Result: Returns only bills where due_amount > 0

Title: Delete bill
Expected Result: Bill deleted, returns {success: true}
